explanation: Because A stays in1 and B cannot share with A or enter2, B is in3. Enumerating the remaining capacity, department and exclusion rules gives exactly four allocations in A,B,C,D,E,F order: (1,3,2,1,3,2), cost9; (1,3,1,2,2,3), cost11; (1,3,2,1,2,3), cost12; (1,3,2,3,2,1), cost14. explanation: If C uses the bench before D, C cannot finish before6 (A4+C2);D then ends no earlier than11 andE no earlier than13. stem: Exactly two of Lockers1–4 contain parcels. Three notices make these claims: A: “Lockers1 AND2 contain parcels.” B: “Exactly one of Lockers2 and3 contains a parcel.” C: “Locker4 contains a parcel.” Exactly two notices are true. Which list gives ALL possible occupied-locker pairs?
explanation: Enumerate all six pairs. {1,2} gives true,true,false;{1,3} gives false,true,false;{1,4} gives false,false,true;{2,3} gives false,false,false;{2,4} gives false,true,true;{3,4} gives false,true,true. Exactly two truths therefore allow only {1,2},{2,4},{3,4}. The alternatives retain some compatible pairs but insert an incompatible one or omit another.

stem: A,B,C,D,E,F attend two sessions, morning and afternoon, exactly three per session and each person once. The FIXED requirements A morning and F afternoon cannot be changed. Four additional rules are R1: B and C attend together; R2: A and D attend different sessions; R3: B and E attend different sessions; R4: E attends an earlier session than C. Exactly ONE additional rule will be removed; all other requirements remain. Which list contains ALL and ONLY the single rules whose removal permits a complete allocation?
explanation: With all rules, R4 forces E morning and C afternoon; R1 adds B afternoon, R2 adds D afternoon and fixed F is also afternoon, exceeding capacity. Removing R2 permits morning A,D,E and afternoon B,C,F. Removing R4 permits morning A,B,C and afternoon D,E,F. Removing R1 still forces E morning/C afternoon through R4, B afternoon through R3 and D afternoon through R2, overfilling with F. Removing R3 leaves B,C,D,F forced afternoon through R1,R2,R4. Thus only R2 and R4 individually repair the system; each requires its own consistent witness.

stem: A directed network has ONLY these links, with their closure costs in budget units: S→A4, S→B3, A→B2, A→C3, B→C2, A→T5, B→T6, C→T4. Travel follows arrows; no reversed links are allowed. At most THREE links may be closed, and S→A and S→B may NOT both be closed. What is the least total closure cost that leaves NO route from S to T?
explanation: A successful cut using at most3 links is one of {S→A,B→C,B→T}, cost4+2+6=12; {S→A,B→T,C→T}, cost14; or {A→T,B→T,C→T}, cost15. To see exhaustion, if S→A is closed, S→B stays open: B→T must close and the B→C→T path requires either B→C or C→T closed. If S→A stays open but S→B closes, the A→T, A→B→T and A→C→T routes require three further closures, exceeding3. If both S exits stay open, the direct A→T and B→T links must close, leaving only one closure to block both paths through C: close C→T. A two-link S-exit cut is forbidden. Thus12 is the minimum, not the cost15 of simply closing every T entrance.

stem: A four-digit code uses1,2,3,4 exactly once. In the reading1234, exactly TWO digits are in their correct positions. In a second reading2314, NO digit is in its correct position. Which list contains ALL possible true codes?
explanation: Exactly two positional matches with1234 mean exactly one pair of its positions was swapped. The six such codes are2134,3214,4231,1324,1432,1243. Compare each against2314:2134 has matching2 inposition1 and4 inposition4;3214 has1 inposition3 and4 inposition4;1324 has3 inposition2 and4 inposition4. The remaining4231,1432,1243 have zero matches. Every offered list preserves two valid candidates but substitutes an invalid third.

stem: Four teams A,B,C,D each play every other team once. A win earns3 points, a draw1 per team, a loss0. Final totals are A6,B4,C5,D1. A beat B; C drew with D. What were the results of A versus C and B versus D?

choices.text: C beat A; B beat D.
A beat C; B beat D.
C beat A; B drew with D.
A drew with C; D beat B.

explanation: A already earned3 againstB; to reach6 over its two remaining matches it must win one and lose one. D has1 from its draw withC, so loses toA andB. Therefore A beatsD, loses toC;B beatsD. C has1 againstD and3 againstA, needing1 againstB;B has0 againstA and3 againstD, also needing1 againstC. Thus all six results consistently produce the totals; options sharing only one correct match fail another team's total.

stem: Each card has one letter on one side and one positive integer on the other. Vowels are A,E,I,O,U. Two claims apply to EVERY card: (1) If its letter is a vowel, its integer is even. (2) If its integer is divisible by3, its letter is a vowel. Four cards show the faces A, T, 6, 7. Which cards must be turned over to test for ALL possible violations of these two claims, turning as few cards as possible?
explanation: A must be checked for an odd integer (violates1). T must be checked for a multiple of3 (violates2). The6 must be checked for a consonant (violates2). The7 must be checked for a vowel (violates1). Each unturned card has a possible hidden violating face compatible with what is visible, so all four are necessary. Checking only the named antecedents would miss contrapositive tests.
